headline: Hyperia City goes on general release while Amber/Emerald finishes the old format on top

tldr.text: Set 14, Hyperia City, went on general release October 23 after prereleases began October 16. It brings in Pixar's Coco and adds the new one-use ink drops mechanic.
The last big pre-Hyperia events (October 10-11) belonged to Amber/Emerald: 3 wins and 8 podium spots across five events, including a full podium sweep at the 142-player CCQ Sevilla.

The first look at the Set 14 meta comes from the Quest World Iconic Clash, a 16-player invitational. Amber/Emerald Songs, Emerald/Amethyst Retro, Emerald/Steel and Amber/Steel Rockstar Stitch are all among the 16 decklists.

Set 15, Into the Inkdark, is due February 12, 2027. It brings Collector Boosters and a new serialized top rarity called Illustrious, sold only through Play Hub stores, Ravensburger's online store and some Disney locations.
Unlike Wilds Unknown and the set before it, Hyperia City is easy to find at or near MSRP in the US, though some players abroad and at certain stores still struggle to get product.

meta.text: Old-format wrap-up (events October 10-11): Amber/Emerald had 3 wins and 8 podiums. It was also the most-played deck at four of the five events, peaking at 34.4% of the field at the Lore Seekers championship and 33.3% at CCQ Sevilla.

Amber/Amethyst had 1 win and 3 podiums, and was the most-played deck in Torino (25.8%). Emerald/Amethyst won the biggest US event, the 138-player Cauldron Cup CCQ. Emerald/Steel had 2 podiums and no wins.

Early Hyperia decks: in the Iconic Clash lists, Amber/Emerald Songs (Bryan Pereira, Jacob Frank, Joseph Quigley) appears three times, and Emerald/Amethyst Retro is played by Alessandro Cavalli and Fungus. Lukas Kaupa brought Emerald/Sapphire and vVonderland played Amber/Steel Rockstar Stitch.

Emerald/Amethyst Retro looks like an early front-runner. Liam Dolecki won an 8-player weekly at Gemini Games on October 21 with it, ahead of Amber/Steel, Amber/Sapphire and Emerald/Steel. Xenulous (Team Maelstrom) also covered the deck on Alter Academy.

New cards drawing attention: Manifest calls Flash a new Steel staple, and a Reddit thread says it's overtuned (2 cost, quests for 2, Resist, and it shuts down Rush). Manifest also rates Max Goof as one of the most powerful cards in the game.
Brews to watch: Podcana built 15 Hyperia decks and asked whether Ruby/Emerald is real, and a Reddit player reports success with Ruby/Emerald Actions. The Lore College says Amber/Ruby got an upgrade.

players.text: Team MILQ took first and second at the 64-player Uninkables Masters II in Torino: _MILQ_SirGrima won on Amber/Emerald over teammate _MILQ_Rama on Steel/Emerald, with ZTL_Utini third.
Idril won the 142-player CCQ Sevilla, leading an all-Amber/Emerald podium with Mushuu Muchacho and PT_GuRu.

Fetty Guap won the 138-player Cauldron Cup $5,000 CCQ on Emerald/Amethyst over PidgeyPotPie (Emerald/Amber) and James Gray II (Emerald/Steel). The next day, Troy won the 33-player $1,000 Runback on Amethyst/Amber.
GoofyBoy won the 32-player Lore Seekers League Season I Championship on Emerald/Amber, ahead of Lorcanaholic and RyanL.

Iconic Clash first-round matches posted this week include Frank Karsten vs Shane Downey (an Emerald/Steel mirror the caster called extremely technical), Fungus vs Ace 103, vVonderland vs Bryan Pereira, Lukas Kaupa vs Carl Go Boom and Mo Shamblin vs Pandemonium Heart.

news.text: Hyperia City (Set 14) has been on general release since October 23. Disney set up virtual queues at Disney Springs and Downtown Disney for the launch because earlier releases drew huge crowds.
Into the Inkdark (Set 15) is set for February 12, 2027, with Collector Boosters and the serialized Illustrious rarity, and new card reveals have started.

The D23 2026 boxes and the foil Pooh playmat are being re-released through an EQL raffle with separate US and EU entries. Rules of Villainy also flagged that the Cauldron Cup CCQ survey closes October 30 and that DLC Tampa tickets are on sale.
Pixelborn Connect now runs in the browser, with ranked webcam games and an option to hide your hand from your opponent while showing it to stream viewers.

community.text: ICL Season 4 Round 6 (Infinity Week) streamed ETB vs Triad and World Class Cards vs Manifest, with decklists posted on inkdecks.

Supply split: US players report Hyperia at or under MSRP and urge others not to overpay. Meanwhile, a player in the Netherlands can only find €75 troves, and other posts complain about stores holding product back or reselling it, including a store accused of faking event results.
A community pull-rate tracker (lorcanapullrates.ink) says early Hyperia rates look the same as Wilds Unknown so far, with less than half as many packs reported.
For deeper early-meta listening: Rules of Villainy covered Brennan DeCandio's Hyperia decks, Manifest discussed its favorite Set 14 cards, and The Illumiteers had Team Descent on.
